placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the north face of blk_south_water_lasalle, the block's South Water Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is the closest line the plat module's own margin allows and is not a measurement of this frontage, and its east wall is fixed by the west wall of recon_1835_blk_south_water_lasalle_d4_02, which it shares a party line with. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at South Water Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.

persons.name: Giles Spring
persons.note: HIS FIRST OFFICE WAS A BARREL-HEAD AND HIS SECOND WAS DESK-ROOM IN CATON'S. The two of them opposed each other in the first larceny case heard before a justice of the peace in July 1833, and Caton's account of hiring out to carry the chain for a surveyor on the North Side that same month - because clients were few, fees small and board bills maturing - is the only description in this dataset of what an educated newcomer actually did for money in the town's first summer. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 2 times: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Spring, Giles” (poll_1834_103, line 272); Poll list of 1835 — “Spring, G.” (poll_1835_075, line 362). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Spring' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json). THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 3 times, as “SPRING GILES”, 1836-06-29 to 1836-09-05: 3 lots in the platted town — lot 4 of block 41 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L4BL41CHIOT, as printed); lot 5 of block 12 in the town the register codes CHIOTV (L5BL12CHIOTV, as printed); lot 6 of block 12 in the town the register codes CHIOTV (L6BL12CHIOTV, as printed), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $5850.00 (ls1465, ls1466, ls1467). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $5850.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: SPRING GILES matches Giles Spring: the forename names Giles Spring of the 1 person of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. frontage.why: T-0078, and the owner's standing ruling of 2026-08-18 with it: "there should be more and denser buildings. this is important." The reference he supplied for this reach — "South Water Street in 1834", the south bank of the Main Branch — shows a CONTINUOUS WORKING ROW: one-storey log and frame buildings shoulder to shoulder facing the river, the street between them and the grassy bank, two-storey frame stores anchoring its east end. This block's anonymous roofs stood seven metres back from that frontage, a full lot apart, each nudged off the line by its own lateral offset and — because the placement rule takes its bearing from the way into the lot — facing the block's interior rather than the river. That is the shape of a distribution across a block, not of a street. They now stand ON the frontage: the line, its bearing and the end they pack back from are read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and this recipe authors no coordinate for any of them. The 1.5 m setback is not a measurement of this frontage — it is the closest line the plat module's own lot margin allows, adopted so the street wall is one wall. NO ROOF IS ADDED: the run carries exactly the roofs the schedule dealt this block's frontage lots, with every id, family and dimension the one it already had. What the view drives is the treatment — a row on its line, facing the water — never a coordinate, and the side lot lines the row crosses between its own units were conjectural in every record this generator has ever written.
